decisive_items: Singular and large heterotypic proliferative lymphoid cells
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes were noted in the neck and abdomen regions
response.rationale: Biopsy shows proliferative atypical lymphoid cells, strongly supporting lymphoma. R6 (Hodgkin) is more specific but lacks Reed-Sternberg cells; R1 is the broader, best-supported diagnosis. R2 and R5 rely on imaging only; R3/R4 lack histologic support.

rejected.why: Imaging findings are nonspecific and do not confirm a specific NHL subtype without histologic evidence.
Mediastinal cavities and lung nodules are not specific for sarcoidosis; no granulomas or other supporting findings.
Cavities and nodules could suggest TB, but biopsy shows lymphoid proliferation, not granulomatous inflammation.
Multisystem lesions could be metastatic, but no primary tumor identified and biopsy favors lymphoid neoplasm.
Hodgkin lymphoma requires Reed-Sternberg cells, which are not described; broader lymphoma diagnosis is more appropriate.
